Sandbox_RC_Enabled_tooltip: Master toggle for the Reclaimation mod.
Sandbox_RC_Debug_tooltip: Print [RC] debug traces to the log. Off for normal play.
Sandbox_RC_ClaimsEnabled_tooltip: Allow players to claim vehicles and lock out non-whitelisted players. When off, no vehicle is locked.
Sandbox_RC_MaxClaims_tooltip: How many motor vehicles (cars, trucks, RVs - anything that isn't a trailer) one player may claim at once. Trailers have their own separate cap. 0 = unlimited. Staff are exempt.
Sandbox_RC_MaxClaimTrailers_tooltip: How many trailers one player may claim at once, separate from the vehicle cap - so hitching a camper never costs a car slot. Claimed trailers get the full lock (towing, loot, and RV-interior entry if an RV mod is installed). 0 = unlimited. Staff are exempt.
Sandbox_RC_MaxAllowed_tooltip: How many other players an owner may grant access to on a single vehicle.
Sandbox_RC_ClaimInactivityDays_tooltip: Real-time days a player can be absent before ALL their claims auto-release. 0 = never. Server downtime is credited back so an outage does not mass-expire claims.
Sandbox_RC_ClaimExemptUsers_tooltip: Comma-separated usernames whose claims never expire (e.g. vacations, deployments). Because the Janitor never touches claimed vehicles, these players' cars can never be reclaimed either - a true never-abandoned list. The max-claims cap still applies to them.
Sandbox_RC_AdminOnly_tooltip: When on, only staff can dismantle vehicles. Players keep the vanilla burnt-wreck removal.
Sandbox_RC_EngineThreshold_tooltip: A non-wreck vehicle can only be dismantled while its Engine part condition is BELOW this value - good cars can't be scrapped. Wrecks and trailers are exempt.
Sandbox_RC_EngineTooGoodText_tooltip: The line players see when a good engine blocks dismantling - shown as their character's own thought. Leave blank for the built-in line. Write {threshold} anywhere to insert the threshold number. Capped at 120 characters.
Sandbox_RC_DismantleTimePercent_tooltip: Scales how long dismantling takes. 100 = vanilla burnt-vehicle removal time (still skill-scaled); 200 = twice as long.
Sandbox_RC_RespectClaims_tooltip: A claimed vehicle cannot be dismantled until it is released - including by its owner (release first, then scrap; prevents accidents). Staff override in the field.
Sandbox_RC_RespectPhunZones_tooltip: Honor the per-zone 'No Vehicle Dismantle' flag from PhunZones2, if that mod is installed. Does nothing without it.
Sandbox_RC_EngineLockEnabled_tooltip: Block non-staff players from taking or uninstalling the Engine part, so good vehicles aren't stripped for motor parts. Actual pulls are written to the ledger either way.
Sandbox_RC_JanitorEnabled_tooltip: Truly abandoned vehicles are removed and converted into respawn tokens (contents drop to the ground first - loot is never destroyed). A vehicle is only ever abandoned when the PLAYER is gone: anyone who keeps logging in keeps every vehicle they last used, touched or not. Claimed vehicles, wrecks, and safehouse vehicles are never considered at all.
Sandbox_RC_JanitorAbandonDays_tooltip: REAL days. An unclaimed vehicle is reclaimed only when the last player known to have used it has NOT logged in for this long (logging in alone preserves it - no need to touch the car), or - for vehicles no player was ever seen with - when it has sat unused this long. Server downtime is credited back. Fractions work for testing (0.01 = about 15 minutes). 0 disables the Janitor.
Sandbox_RC_JanitorFeedsBudget_tooltip: Upper bound on vehicles reclaimed in one hourly sweep. Keeps a backlog (e.g. after long downtime) draining gradually instead of vanishing a parking lot at once, and caps the token mint rate.
Sandbox_RC_SpawnerEnabled_tooltip: Enable the staff vehicle spawner (configure in a window, then click the world to place). Every spawn - and every denied attempt - is written to the ledger.
Sandbox_RC_SpawnerAccess_tooltip: Which staff ranks may use the vehicle spawner. The server checks the SENDER's access level on every spawn command - hiding the buttons is cosmetic, this setting is the real gate.
Sandbox_RC_SpawnerMissingPartsMax_toolti: Upper bound on how many parts the 'Missing parts' tick strips from a manually-spawned vehicle. Each spawn rolls a random 1..this many (capped at the parts the vehicle actually has). The engine is never eligible. Affects ONLY vehicles placed through the staff spawner - never world, player, or reclaimed vehicles.
Sandbox_RC_NoVanillaVehicles_tooltip: Vanilla drivable vehicles no longer spawn on the map: parking stalls, traffic jams, dealership lots, business fleets. Applies from the very first chunk of a fresh world; on an existing world only not-yet-visited areas are affected and nothing already spawned is removed. Burnt/smashed wrecks and trailers still spawn, and vehicles added by mods are untouched - including packs that register under the Base module. Story set-pieces are handled by the option below.
Sandbox_RC_NoVanillaStoryVehicles: Story Vehicles Spawn As Burnt Hulls
Sandbox_RC_NoVanillaStoryVehicles_toolti: Randomized stories that hardcode a vanilla vehicle (police blockades, crash scenes, camps, sieges) spawn the burnt hull of that vehicle instead, so the scene keeps its shape without gifting a drivable car. Modded vehicles - including story-swap mods that redirect to a vehicle pack - are never touched, and neither are staff-spawner vehicles. To remove the scenes entirely, use the vanilla 'Vehicle Story' / 'Zone Story' frequency options instead.
Sandbox_RC_RespawnEnabled_tooltip: Vehicles that leave the world come back somewhere useful. Reclaimed, dismantled and destroyed vehicles mint respawn tokens; each hour a metered number of those tokens are spent placing fresh vehicles near players. Fleet size stays roughly flat, but the fleet MIGRATES out of dead corners of the map and back to where people are actually playing. Placements only ever land in real parking areas - never on grass - and never inside a safehouse.
Sandbox_RC_RespawnPerSweep_tooltip: Upper bound on vehicles placed in one hourly sweep. This is a ceiling, not a quota: a placement only happens if a token is available AND somewhere legal to park is loaded nearby, so the real rate is usually lower. 0 pauses placement while still banking tokens, so you can let a pool build and then open the tap.
Sandbox_RC_RespawnMinDistance_tooltip: Tiles. A replacement never appears closer than this to the player it was placed for, so cars are never seen popping into existence. Roughly 40 is just beyond comfortable view distance.
Sandbox_RC_RespawnMaxDistance_tooltip: Tiles. How far out to search for a legal parking spot before giving up for this sweep. In practice the edge of the loaded map usually stops the search first - vehicles can only be placed in streamed-in chunks - which is what keeps replacements tracking the active play area.
Sandbox_RC_RespawnModdedOnly_tooltip: The lifecycle never places a vanilla vehicle. Use this when you run vehicle packs and have suppressed vanilla map spawns, so the respawner cannot quietly reintroduce the fleet you just removed. Vehicles registered by mods under the Base module still count as modded - the test is which mod first defined the vehicle, not what it is named. Turn off to let the lifecycle draw from everything installed.
Sandbox_RC_RespawnCondition_tooltip: Part wear on placed vehicles. Fuel and battery charge are always rolled independently, and replacements never come with a key in the glovebox - a vehicle the world put back is something to find and get running, not a delivery.
Sandbox_RC_RespawnOnDestruction_tooltip: A vehicle wrecked by fire or collision counts as leaving the fleet and mints a replacement token, alongside the tokens from Janitor reclamation and field dismantle. The replacement goes to the world, not to whoever lost the vehicle, so destroying your own car is not a way to farm new ones. Turn off if you want only reclamation and dismantle to feed the pool.
